digitisation.method: crimson boundary wash extracted as a barrier mask (R-G>28, R-B>34, R>120), dilated to close gaps, then a 4-connected flood fill seeded on the Berlin symbol inside the engraved field
digitisation.result: the fill escaped and covered 97.7% of the field
digitisation.diagnosis: the Brandenburg boundary on this plate is drawn as a DASHED crimson line with a discontinuous wash; a 7-px dilation does not close every gap, and larger dilations begin to swallow the boundary's own neighbourhood
digitisation.second_attempt: all saturated colour treated as barrier, at four threshold/dilation combinations
digitisation.second_result: the aged paper is itself tinted, so every threshold that closed the dashes also walled off the interior (fill collapsed to 33-362 px)
digitisation.stage_decision: Digitisation was stopped rather than forced. Producing a polygon by relaxing the colour rule, or by tracing one sheet from the other, would have violated the stage's own constraints; producing one by hand within the remaining budget would have put the rest of the stage at risk.

digitisation.method: not attempted: the BnF attempt was the cheaper of the two and its failure mode (discontinuous boundary rendering plus a tinted ground) applies at least as strongly here, where the Kreis washes are pastel and the neighbours carry thin coloured edge stripes of similar hue
